criteria.text: The response concludes that Amendment No. 1 narrows the liability-cap carve-out so that Broumoux's recall-cost indemnity (Distribution Agreement Section 10.1(c)) becomes subject to the $750,000 cap, while Paikort's own Section 10.2 indemnities remain uncapped.
The response locates the recall-indemnity cap issue in Amendment No. 1, Section 3 (the restated Section 11.3(b)).
The response explains why the capping of Broumoux's recall-cost indemnity matters to Paikort.
The response recommends a fix for the capping of Broumoux's recall-cost indemnity.

The response concludes that the Quality Agreement selects New Jersey law and exclusive Essex County, New Jersey courts for recall and handling disputes, displacing the Distribution Agreement's Delaware law and New Castle County forum for those disputes.
hints: laws of the State of New Jersey

criteria.text: The response locates the governing law and forum conflict in Quality Agreement Section 12.
The response explains why the New Jersey law and forum clause for recall disputes matters to Paikort.
The response recommends a fix for the governing law and forum conflict over recall disputes.
The response concludes that the pending Fenwyck merger is a Change of Control of Paikort that requires Broumoux's prior written consent, and that this consent has not been obtained or waived.
The response locates the change-of-control consent issue in Distribution Agreement Section 14.2.
The response explains why the missing change-of-control consent matters to Paikort.
The response recommends a fix for the missing change-of-control consent.
The response states that the Distribution Agreement's aggregate liability cap is $750,000.
The response states that Amendment No. 1 prevails over the Distribution Agreement in the event of conflict.
The response is organized as a memo that lists issues individually and flags urgent matters at or near the top.
The response briefly identifies the Wilmington office lease as having no bearing on the distribution relationship.
The response claims that Amendment No. 1 contains or constitutes Broumoux's consent to, or waiver of, the Change of Control from the Fenwyck merger.
The response claims that, after Amendment No. 1, Broumoux's recall-cost indemnity under Section 10.1(c) remains excluded from the liability cap.
